dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the instrument tray and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The appointment book review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Long single procedures never trouble my forearm; one deep cleaning in a stretch is easy.
Single sustained cases are fine.
Fine and familiar.
Someone new shadowed me in the hygiene operatory this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the patient turnover into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
With ten-minute spacing between patients my forearm stays quiet all week; the spacing is when the tendon actually recovers.
The gaps are doing the work.
The gaps are the treatment plan, effectively.
Admin afternoons between patients give my hands all the recovery they need.
Mixed days manage themselves.
They always have.
I archived last cycle's notes on the appointment book and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My occupational health review recorded forearm tendinopathy and recommended micro-breaks between instrument-heavy appointments.
A documented condition with a documented mitigation.
Both on file.
A vendor call about the instrument tray ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the hygiene operatory checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the patient turnover.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the appointment book records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The one compressed morning I covered, eight scaling patients back to back with no buffers, my forearm was burning by patient six and I had to book physio that evening.
Back-to-back load triggered it within one morning.
Within one morning, reliably.
I sketched next week's plan for the patient turnover before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the instrument tray updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The compressed-schedule pilot removes all buffers to add two patients per day, and joining it is this month's decision.
The pilot is exactly the trigger format.
Exactly, and for a full month.
I compared two options for the appointment book tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the hygiene operatory handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
If I join the compressed-schedule pilot next month, how will my first two weeks realistically go?
